title: Impact of global climate change induced variations in reservoir-river systems on fish habitats
abstract: Global climate change (GCC) and reservoir operations impact basin-scale hydrological conditions, altering river-scale hydrodynamics and aquatic habitats. This study designed a numerical evaluation methodology framework that integrates GCC, downscaling, hydrological, hydrodynamic, water temperature (WT), and habitat suitability models across global, basin, river, and habitat to predict the impacts of GCC on the hydrology and aquatic ecological environment of the reservoir-river system (RRS). The framework was applied to the Xiaolangdi Reservoir (XLDR) and its downstream river reach. In the study area, runoff, water level, WT, and weighted usable area (WUA) were predicted for the baseline and four scenarios, and the impact of GCC on the inflow, WT, and WUA of the RRS was evaluated. The results proved that the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) model, the statistical downscaling model (SDSM), three-dimensional (3D) and two-dimensional (2D) hydrodynamic, and WT models met requirements. Runoff remained sufficient to meet system demands under the four GCC scenarios. WT surface, middle, and bottom in the XLDR showed increasing trends. Compared to the baseline scenario, the decrease in WUA for the spawning and juvenile Yellow River carp (Cyprinus carpio haematopterus) (YRC) was mainly influenced by hydrodynamic conditions and rising WT changes. The impacts of GCC were likely to exacerbate the adverse effects of reservoir regulation on YRC’s breeding season.
field: Climate change impacts on fish habitats
problem: Accurately predicting the combined impacts of global climate change and reservoir operations on fish habitats is challenging because the effects are complex, and individual models are insufficient for bridging the multiple spatial scales from global climate to local river conditions, necessitating an integrated, multi-model approach.
method: This study proposes a coupled modeling framework integrating climate, hydrological, hydrodynamic, and habitat suitability models to predict the impacts of global climate change on fish habitats in reservoir-river systems.
task: The task is to predict the impacts of global climate change on the hydrology and fish habitats of a reservoir-river system by applying a coupled numerical framework that integrates hydrological, hydrodynamic, water temperature, and habitat suitability models.
innovation: This paper presents a coupled numerical framework integrating global climate change, downscaling, hydrological, hydrodynamic, water temperature, and habitat models to quantitatively assess the impacts of climate change on fish habitats within reservoir-river systems.
